{"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1788747752437,"sessionID":"ses_f8656223bffeD3dPw3uPxq2lU9","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"Czel9QBknjA9otSi","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"filePath":"/app/signal_analysis.py","content":"#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"\nSensor Signal Analysis and Filtering Script\n\nThis script loads a sensor signal (time and amplitude) from a CSV file, estimates\nthe sampling frequency, applies a fourth-order low-pass Butterworth filter,\ncomputes summary statistics, generates waveform and FFT plots, and saves the\nfiltered signal to an output CSV file.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport os\nimport sys\nimport argparse\nfrom typing import Tuple, Dict, Any\n\nimport numpy as np\nimport pandas as pd\nfrom scipy import signal\nimport matplotlib\n# Use non-interactive backend for headless environments and reliable file saving\nmatplotlib.use('Agg')\nimport matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n\n\ndef parse_arguments() -> argparse.Namespace:\n    \"\"\"Parse command-line arguments.\"\"\"\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=\"Filter and analyze a recorded sensor signal.\")\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"--input\", \"-i\",\n        type=str,\n        default=\"data/input_signal.csv\",\n        help=\"Path to input CSV signal file (default: data/input_signal.csv)\"\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"--output-dir\", \"-o\",\n        type=str,\n        default=\"output\",\n        help=\"Directory to save filtered data and plots (default: output)\"\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"--cutoff\", \"-c\",\n        type=float,\n        default=20.0,\n        help=\"Low-pass filter cutoff frequency in Hz (default: 20.0)\"\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"--order\",\n        type=int,\n        default=4,\n        help=\"Butterworth filter order (default: 4)\"\n    )\n    return parser.parse_args()\n\n\ndef load_and_validate_signal(filepath: str) -> pd.DataFrame:\n    \"\"\"\n    Load a sensor signal from CSV and validate its structure and contents.\n    \n    Args:\n        filepath: Path to the CSV file.\n        \n    Returns:\n        pd.DataFrame containing validated 'time' and 'amplitude' columns.\n        \n    Raises:\n        FileNotFoundError: If the input CSV file does not exist.\n        ValueError: If columns are invalid, data contains NaNs, or data is insufficient.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not os.path.exists(filepath):\n        raise FileNotFoundError(f\"Input file not found: {filepath}\")\n    \n    try:\n        df = pd.read_csv(filepath)\n    except Exception as e:\n        raise ValueError(f\"Failed to read CSV file '{filepath}': {e}\") from e\n\n    # Clean column names by stripping whitespace\n    df.columns = [str(col).strip() for col in df.columns]\n    \n    required_cols = {'time', 'amplitude'}\n    if not required_cols.issubset(df.columns):\n        raise ValueError(\n            f\"Invalid columns in {filepath}. Expected columns 'time' and 'amplitude', \"\n            f\"but found: {list(df.columns)}\"\n        )\n    \n    # Check for missing/NaN values\n    if df[['time', 'amplitude']].isnull().any().any():\n        raise ValueError(\"Data contains missing (NaN) values in 'time' or 'amplitude' columns.\")\n    \n    # Check for valid numeric types\n    try:\n        df['time'] = pd.to_numeric(df['time'], errors='raise')\n        df['amplitude'] = pd.to_numeric(df['amplitude'], errors='raise')\n    except Exception as e:\n        raise ValueError(\"Non-numeric values encountered in 'time' or 'amplitude' columns.\") from e\n\n    # Check for sufficient data\n    if len(df) < 15:\n        raise ValueError(f\"Insufficient data: signal must contain at least 15 samples, but has {len(df)}.\")\n    \n    # Check that time intervals are valid and strictly increasing\n    time_diffs = np.diff(df['time'].values)\n    if (time_diffs <= 0).any():\n        raise ValueError(\"Time column must be strictly increasing with positive time steps.\")\n        \n    return df\n\n\ndef estimate_sampling_frequency(time_series: np.ndarray) -> float:\n    \"\"\"\n    Estimate the sampling frequency (Hz) from a time series array.\n    \n    Args:\n        time_series: Array of timestamps in seconds.\n        \n    Returns:\n        Estimated sampling frequency in Hz.\n        \n    Raises:\n        ValueError: If time series has insufficient points or invalid intervals.\n    \"\"\"\n    if len(time_series) < 2:\n        raise ValueError(\"Insufficient data to estimate sampling frequency.\")\n    \n    time_diffs = np.diff(time_series)\n    median_dt = float(np.median(time_diffs))\n    \n    if median_dt <= 0:\n        raise ValueError(\"Invalid time intervals: median dt is zero or negative.\")\n        \n    fs = 1.0 / median_dt\n    return fs\n\n\ndef apply_lowpass_filter(\n    data: np.ndarray,\n    fs: float,\n    cutoff: float = 20.0,\n    order: int = 4\n) -> np.ndarray:\n    \"\"\"\n    Apply a zero-phase fourth-order low-pass Butterworth filter.\n    \n    Args:\n        data: Input signal amplitude array.\n        fs: Sampling frequency in Hz.\n        cutoff: Cutoff frequency in Hz (default: 20.0).\n        order: Filter order (default: 4).\n        \n    Returns:\n        Filtered signal array preserving original time alignment.\n        \n    Raises:\n        ValueError: If cutoff is above Nyquist frequency or signal is too short.\n    \"\"\"\n    nyquist = 0.5 * fs\n    if cutoff >= nyquist:\n        raise ValueError(\n            f\"Cutoff frequency ({cutoff} Hz) must be strictly less than the \"\n            f\"Nyquist frequency ({nyquist:.2f} Hz for fs={fs:.2f} Hz).\"\n        )\n    \n    min_len = order * 3 + 1\n    if len(data) < min_len:\n        raise ValueError(f\"Signal length ({len(data)}) is too short for filter order {order} (minimum {min_len}).\")\n    \n    # Normalize cutoff frequency by Nyquist frequency\n    normal_cutoff = cutoff / nyquist\n    b, a = signal.butter(N=order, Wn=normal_cutoff, btype='low', analog=False)\n    \n    # Use zero-phase forward-backward filtering to preserve original time alignment\n    filtered_data = signal.filtfilt(b, a, data)\n    return filtered_data\n\n\ndef compute_fft(amplitude: np.ndarray, fs: float) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:\n    \"\"\"\n    Compute the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) magnitude spectrum of a real-valued signal.\n    \n    Args:\n        amplitude: Signal amplitude array.\n        fs: Sampling frequency in Hz.\n        \n    Returns:\n        Tuple of (frequencies array, normalized magnitude spectrum array).\n    \"\"\"\n    n = len(amplitude)\n    if n == 0:\n        raise ValueError(\"Cannot compute FFT on an empty signal.\")\n    \n    freqs = np.fft.rfftfreq(n, d=1.0 / fs)\n    mag = np.abs(np.fft.rfft(amplitude)) * (2.0 / n)\n    \n    # Adjust DC component (0 Hz) and Nyquist frequency normalization\n    if n > 0:\n        mag[0] = mag[0] / 2.0\n        if n % 2 == 0 and len(mag) > 1:\n            mag[-1] = mag[-1] / 2.0\n            \n    return freqs, mag\n\n\ndef compute_dominant_frequency(freqs: np.ndarray, mag: np.ndarray, ignore_dc: bool = True) -> float:\n    \"\"\"\n    Find the dominant frequency (frequency with highest FFT magnitude).\n    \n    Args:\n        freqs: Array of frequency bins.\n        mag: Array of FFT magnitudes.\n        ignore_dc: If True, ignores the 0 Hz DC offset bin.\n        \n    Returns:\n        Dominant frequency in Hz.\n    \"\"\"\n    if len(freqs) == 0 or len(mag) == 0:\n        raise ValueError(\"Empty frequency or magnitude arrays.\")\n    \n    if ignore_dc and len(freqs) > 1:\n        valid_mask = freqs > 0.0\n        if np.any(valid_mask):\n            peak_idx = np.argmax(mag[valid_mask])\n            return float(freqs[valid_mask][peak_idx])\n            \n    return float(freqs[np.argmax(mag)])\n\n\ndef compute_signal_statistics(\n    time_series: np.ndarray,\n    amplitude: np.ndarray,\n    fs: float\n) -> Dict[str, float]:\n    \"\"\"\n    Compute summary statistics for a signal.\n    \n    Args:\n        time_series: Array of timestamps in seconds.\n        amplitude: Signal amplitude array.\n        fs: Sampling frequency in Hz.\n        \n    Returns:\n        Dictionary containing duration_sec, mean, min, max, and dominant_freq_hz.\n    \"\"\"\n    duration = float(time_series[-1] - time_series[0])\n    mean_val = float(np.mean(amplitude))\n    min_val = float(np.min(amplitude))\n    max_val = float(np.max(amplitude))\n    \n    freqs, mag = compute_fft(amplitude, fs)\n    dom_freq = compute_dominant_frequency(freqs, mag, ignore_dc=True)\n    \n    return {\n        \"duration_sec\": duration,\n        \"mean\": mean_val,\n        \"min\": min_val,\n        \"max\": max_val,\n        \"dominant_freq_hz\": dom_freq\n    }\n\n\ndef print_statistics_report(\n    fs: float,\n    raw_stats: Dict[str, float],\n    filtered_stats: Dict[str, float]\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Print formatted summary statistics for both raw and filtered signals.\"\"\"\n    print(\"=\" * 64)\n    print(\"                 SIGNAL ANALYSIS REPORT                 \")\n    print(\"=\" * 64)\n    print(f\"Estimated Sampling Frequency : {fs:.4f} Hz\")\n    print(\"-\" * 64)\n    print(f\"{'Statistic':<26} | {'Raw Signal':<15} | {'Filtered Signal':<15}\")\n    print(\"-\" * 64)\n    print(f\"{'Duration (sec)':<26} | {raw_stats['duration_sec']:<15.4f} | {filtered_stats['duration_sec']:<15.4f}\")\n    print(f\"{'Mean Amplitude':<26} | {raw_stats['mean']:<15.4f} | {filtered_stats['mean']:<15.4f}\")\n    print(f\"{'Minimum Amplitude':<26} | {raw_stats['min']:<15.4f} | {filtered_stats['min']:<15.4f}\")\n    print(f\"{'Maximum Amplitude':<26} | {raw_stats['max']:<15.4f} | {filtered_stats['max']:<15.4f}\")\n    print(f\"{'Dominant Frequency (Hz)':<26} | {raw_stats['dominant_freq_hz']:<15.2f} | {filtered_stats['dominant_freq_hz']:<15.2f}\")\n    print(\"=\" * 64)\n\n\ndef plot_raw_signal(\n    time_series: np.ndarray,\n    raw_amplitude: np.ndarray,\n    output_path: str\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Plot and save the raw signal waveform.\"\"\"\n    plt.figure(figsize=(10, 4))\n    plt.plot(time_series, raw_amplitude, color='#1f77b4', linewidth=1.0, label='Raw Signal')\n    plt.xlabel('Time (s)')\n    plt.ylabel('Amplitude')\n    plt.title('Raw Sensor Signal')\n    plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)\n    plt.legend(loc='upper right')\n    plt.tight_layout()\n    plt.savefig(output_path, dpi=300)\n    plt.close()\n\n\ndef plot_signal_comparison(\n    time_series: np.ndarray,\n    raw_amplitude: np.ndarray,\n    filtered_amplitude: np.ndarray,\n    cutoff: float,\n    output_path: str\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Plot and save the raw and filtered signals together.\"\"\"\n    plt.figure(figsize=(10, 5))\n    plt.plot(time_series, raw_amplitude, color='gray', linewidth=1.0, alpha=0.6, label='Raw Signal')\n    plt.plot(\n        time_series,\n        filtered_amplitude,\n        color='#d62728',\n        linewidth=1.5,\n        label=f'Filtered Signal ({cutoff} Hz Cutoff)'\n    )\n    plt.xlabel('Time (s)')\n    plt.ylabel('Amplitude')\n    plt.title('Raw vs. Filtered Sensor Signal Comparison')\n    plt.grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)\n    plt.legend(loc='upper right')\n {"type":"tool_use","timestamp":1788747798588,"sessionID":"ses_f8656223bffeD3dPw3uPxq2lU9","part":{"type":"tool","tool":"write","callID":"PiAHYK3OAiCkhNu2","state":{"status":"completed","input":{"content":"# Sensor Signal Analysis\n\nA Python tool for filtering and analyzing recorded time-series sensor signals. It loads raw time and amplitude data from a CSV file, estimates the sampling frequency, applies a zero-phase fourth-order low-pass Butterworth filter, generates comprehensive visualizations, and reports summary statistics.\n\n## Features\n\n- **Sampling Frequency Estimation**: Calculates the sampling rate automatically from the time intervals.\n- **Zero-Phase Digital Filtering**: Applies a fourth-order Butterworth low-pass filter (default 20 Hz cutoff) using `filtfilt` to prevent phase distortion and preserve exact timestamp alignment.\n- **Summary Statistics**: Computes duration, mean, minimum, maximum, and dominant frequency (using Fast Fourier Transform) for both raw and filtered signals.\n- **Visualizations**: Produces high-resolution waveform plots and FFT magnitude spectra.\n- **Data Export**: Saves the filtered time-series data to a clean CSV file.\n- **Input Validation**: Verifies file existence, column structure, data sufficiency, and timestamp monotonicity.\n\n## Installation\n\n1. Ensure you have Python 3.8 or newer installed.\n2. (Optional but recommended) Create and activate a Python virtual environment:\n   ```bash\n   python3 -m venv venv\n   source venv/bin/activate  # On Windows use: venv\\Scripts\\activate\n   ```\n3. Install the required dependencies:\n   ```bash\n   pip install -r requirements.txt\n   ```\n\n## Usage\n\n### Basic Usage\n\nRun the analysis script with default settings (processes `data/input_signal.csv` and saves outputs to `output/`):\n\n```bash\npython signal_analysis.py\n```\n\n### Advanced Usage\n\nYou can customize input/output paths and filter parameters using command-line arguments:\n\n```bash\npython signal_analysis.py --input data/my_signal.csv --output-dir results --cutoff 30.0 --order 4\n```\n\n### Command-Line Arguments\n\n- `-i, --input`: Path to the input CSV file (default: `data/input_signal.csv`). The CSV must contain `time` and `amplitude` columns.\n- `-o, --output-dir`: Directory where filtered data and plots will be saved (default: `output`).\n- `-c, --cutoff`: Low-pass filter cutoff frequency in Hz (default: `20.0`).\n- `--order`: Butterworth filter order (default: `4`).\n\n## Output Artifacts\n\nWhen executed, the script creates the specified output directory (default `output/`) containing:\n\n1. `filtered_signal.csv`: The filtered signal preserving the original time values with columns `time` and `filtered_amplitude`.\n2. `raw_signal.png`: Waveform plot of the raw sensor signal.\n3. `raw_and_filtered_signals.png`: Comparison plot displaying raw and filtered signals together.\n4. `fft_magnitude.png`: Frequency spectrum plot comparing the FFT magnitudes and highlighting the filter cutoff.\n","filePath":"/app/README.md"},"output":"Wrote file successfully.","metadata":{"diagnostics":{},"filepath":"/app/README.md","exists":false,"truncated":false},"title":"README.md","time":{"start":1788747798573,"end":1788747798582}},"metadata":{"google":{"thoughtSignature":"EpcBCpQBARFNMg/NwEUDKdxVqOiZvF3MAZ1J1+ybUZIy4A+ibOkMccsONEI2PmOmv3KxdHDVb+oKXNElDlmhFn0J7BSm0biU2TISaZJRMkt+nzfXUy21x7RQzfzohXcPsLuwDPgHbk8ncQLPUCFjPDJD6UTbg83t9ph7qLLnTL37k+l+VYLmKa2LA+aSEBdSLkXwfHArarNXag=="}},"id":"prt_079ad5824001Ab0hFRjUdcb6Wq","sessionID":"ses_f8656223bffeD3dPw3uPxq2lU9","messageID":"msg_079ad4248001dPLbWYRbrWYlxT"}}
